intro: Build the sentence. Drag each piece into the blank where it belongs.

blanks.label: what it shows, in your words

tiles.text: the railway moved raw cotton from the port to the mills by steam
the railway opened on September 15, 1830, and ran about 30 miles
George and Robert Stephenson built a locomotive called the Rocket
Manchester's mills could get cotton cheaply and make more cloth to sell
railways were an important kind of transportation at the time
Liverpool is a large port city in the northwest of England

correct_sentence: This shows the railway moved raw cotton from the port to the mills by steam, which matters because Manchester's mills could get cotton cheaply and make more cloth to sell.
rationale: The first blank has to be what the evidence means, not the date and the mileage. The second has to reach the mills. Every wrong tile is true, and none of them explains anything.
hints: “Opened on September 15, 1830” is the evidence, not what it shows.
Why it matters has to matter to Britain's factories.

documents.source_document: Document 10 — The Liverpool and Manchester Railway
documents.source_citation: Sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica and Wikipedia, “Liverpool and Manchester Railway” (adapted)
documents.source_text: The Liverpool and Manchester Railway opened on September 15, 1830. It ran about 30 miles between the port of Liverpool and the mill town of Manchester. It was the first railway to run scheduled passenger and freight trains pulled only by steam locomotives. Huge loads of raw materials for the textile mills came into Liverpool by ship and went on by rail.
